provenance: This is capture-analysis data and belongs to the packet-capture indexing and network-forensics category — the Arkime/Moloch, CloudShark, Wireshark, ExtraHop family, together with the trace-replay tooling (tcpreplay-style) those consoles wrap. What led there: the top-level unit is a session keyed by session_id whose protocol is drawn from tcp|udp; each session carries an array of frames, and a frame carries a monotonic tick, a message_id, a fragment_index against a fragment_count, and a payload_hex that is lowercase and even-length — i.e. a byte dump. Fragment index/count with a whole-message drop when any fragment is absent is stream reassembly, and an ordering that dispatches by tick then by a fixed protocol priority is a replay scheduler draining a capture. Sessions, frames, reassembly and byte panes are the vocabulary of a capture console; nothing here reads as a message broker, a job queue or an issue tracker. The policy object is a saved reassembly/replay profile of exactly the kind those consoles keep in a profile library, and the contract and edge-case checklist are the replay engine's format reference and regression suite.
reference_products: Wireshark 4.x desktop analyzer (wireshark.org user's guide, main window / details pane / bytes pane) -- the market leader and the source of nearly every convention in this category. Contributed: the display-filter bar pinned above the content with a validity tint and an 'Apply a display filter ...' placeholder; the packet-list column set (No. / Time / Source / Destination / Protocol / Length / Info) where Time is a monotonic offset in seconds since the start of the capture, not a wall clock -- the direct analog of `tick`; Protocol as a short uppercase token in its own narrow column; Info as a free-text summary column that eats the remaining width and carries strings like '[TCP segment of a reassembled PDU]'; the indented disclosure-triangle detail tree with `Label: value` nodes and [bracketed] generated fields; the offset/hex/ASCII byte pane; and the bottom status bar reading 'Packets: 10299 - Displayed: 10299 (100.0%) - Load time: 0:0.182 - Profile: Default'.

Arkime (Moloch) 5.x session console (arkime.com Sessions, Session Detail and SPIView screenshots, light default theme) -- the reference for the *web* version of the same job, and the closest match for a session index over a stored capture set. Contributed: the dark top nav strip of bare word tabs (Sessions / SPIView / SPIGraph / Connections / Hunt / Files / Stats / History / Settings) with a version string at the far right; the stacked query chrome (search row, then time-window row with Start/End/Bounding/Interval and a blue elapsed-duration readout, then a pale strip carrying page size and the plain-text 'Showing 1 - 260 of 260 entries' count); the convention that every queryable cell value is rendered as a blue link so it can be pushed back into the filter; the green '+' expander in the leading column of each row; the session-detail page built as collapsible white cards on a pale canvas, each with a flat grey header band, a right-aligned label column of small bordered dropdown chips, and blue values; and the SPIView accordion of lowercase category names (general / bgp / cert / cloud) with superscript occurrence counts on each value.

CloudShark Enterprise by QA Cafe (qacafe.com product pages and support.qacafe.com user guide: Capture File Index, Profiles) -- the browser-native rendering of the Wireshark view, and the reference for the surfaces Wireshark has no equivalent of. Contributed: the capture file index as a sortable dense table where clicking a column header sorts and a second click reverses, 30 rows per page, a row click opening the 'decoder window'; the pinned/removable search-filter list above the index rather than a single free-text box; the *profile* as a first-class saved record -- named, described, owned or shared, with built-in profiles unmodifiable -- that governs reassembly preferences, decode-as rules and column layout, which is exactly the shape of this environment's replay profile library; and the documentation chrome itself (navy top bar, left rail of bold section headings with indented children and a grey pill on the active item, breadcrumb above the page title, right-hand on-this-page index) for the format-reference and regression-suite surfaces.

design_tokens.palette: Near-white application canvas (#f4f6f7 to #eef2f3, faintly cool/mint rather than pure grey), white content surfaces sitting on it with a 1px #d8dde1 hairline and no shadow. One dark chrome band: the top nav is near-black #1f2124 (Arkime) or deep navy #12304f (CloudShark docs), white labels at 85% opacity, the active tab a slightly lighter block of the same hue -- never a coloured underline. Exactly one blue does all the work: #2a6ebb / #1a5490 for links, field values, breadcrumbs and the count readout. Body text #212529, secondary #6c757d, table header text #495057. Table header band #e9ecef, zebra rows white / #f7f8f9, hover #eef4fa, selected row a solid #2a6ebb with white text (the only saturated fill in the table). Primary action is a single filled button -- Arkime uses a muted green #5cb85c for Search, everything else is an outlined white button with a #ced4da border. Status colour appears ONLY as a desaturated full-row background wash carrying meaning, never as a pill or a chip: delivered rows stay white, dropped rows get a pale amber #fff6e5, invalid/rejected gets pale red #fdecea with #a02c2c text -- these are colouring *rules*, the way a capture tool tints a packet list, so at most 2-3 rows in a screenful are tinted and the rest is plain. No gradients, no coloured icons, no accent bars, no dark mode. The world-map and histogram furniture in Arkime is entirely greyscale (#8a8a80 bars on white) with the selected time span washed in pale straw #fdf6dd -- charts carry no hue at all.
design_tokens.typography: One UI sans throughout -- -apple-system / 'Segoe UI' / Helvetica Neue / Arial -- at 13px/1.4 for tables and 14px/1.5 for prose; this is a 13px product, not a 16px one. Column headers 12px, 500 weight, sentence case ('Start Time', 'Fragment Index'), not uppercase and not letter-spaced. Section and card titles are large but LIGHT (20-24px, weight 300-400) rather than small and bold -- Arkime's card headers and category headings are the model. Any byte, hash, offset, session key, message id or hex payload is monospace -- SF Mono / Menlo / Consolas / 'DejaVu Sans Mono' -- at 12px, and hex is always lowercase to match payload_hex. Integer counts are tabular-figure and right-aligned with comma grouping over 999 (3,245,118); tick values are bare integers, left-aligned, no unit suffix. Protocol renders as a short lowercase token (tcp, udp) in its own narrow column, exactly as it appears in the data.
design_tokens.density: Dense. Table rows are 28-32px single-line (a wrapped two-value cell may reach ~44px), 6px vertical / 10px horizontal cell padding, 1px #eceff1 row rule or zebra striping but no vertical grid lines inside the body -- vertical rules appear only in the header band. 30 rows per page is the default page size and 500 is offered; the whole point is fitting a screenful of frames without scrolling. Every column header carries a sort caret and is clickable, second click reverses. Form controls are 30-32px tall, inputs are white with a #ced4da border and 3px radius. Cards are the only generous thing on the page: 16px internal padding, 12px between them. Nothing is centred, nothing is full-bleed except the chrome bands.
design_tokens.components: Display-filter bar: a full-width monospace input with a placeholder in filter syntax, an inline submit control at the right edge, and a saved-filter/expression affordance beside it; tint the field pale green when the expression parses and pale red when it does not. Result-count header: a thin pale band directly under the query chrome carrying plain sentence text -- 'Showing 1-30 of 412 sessions' / 'Showing 177 entries filtered from 4,969 total entries' -- in blue on mint; this is the affordance the operator uses to know the population is complete, so it is text, not a badge. Dense table: sortable headers, a leading narrow column for a row expander or index, blue-linked values, no action column of icon buttons. Field/value card: a white card with a flat grey header band, light-weight title, chevron to collapse; inside, a right-aligned label column (bold text, or a small bordered white pill with a caret when the field is queryable) against a left-aligned blue value column, with several bold-label/blue-value pairs allowed to run inline on one line ('Packets 7  Bytes 998  Databytes 524'). Byte pane: three fixed monospace columns -- 8-digit hex offset in navy, then 16 hex byte pairs split into two 8-byte groups by a wider gap, then an ASCII gutter also split 8+8 with '.' for non-printables -- no borders, no zebra, selected bytes inverted to white-on-blue. Detail tree: indented rows with disclosure triangles, 'Label: value' where the label is plain and the value follows the colon, generated/derived fields in [square brackets] and a lighter tint. Reference document: a sequential prose page with a breadcrumb, a heading, body copy at 14px, definition-style tables, and prev/next page links at the foot -- no jump index. Regression suite: cases as a flat table of id / kind / expectation, expectation rendered as monospace ('ValueError') or short sentence, kind chosen from a two-item segmented control. Buttons: one filled primary per surface, everything else outlined; small paired dark/blue button groups ('Unload All' / 'Load All') sit right-aligned in section header bands.
design_tokens.spacing: 8px base unit. Left rail 200-240px fixed, full height, white or #f8f9fa with a #dee2e6 right hairline. Top chrome is a stack of full-bleed bands with no page margin: nav (44px) then filter bar (44px) then time/scope row (36px) then count strip (28px) -- they butt directly against each other with 1px separators, and the table starts immediately below with no gap. Content well is capped around 1400px with 16-24px side padding; the format-reference prose pages cap much narrower, ~760px, and left-align rather than centre. Card grid is two columns at >=1200px, one below. Table-to-table vertical rhythm is 16px; heading to its content is 8px. There is no whitespace between the chrome and the data -- the visual generosity in this category all lives inside the cards, never between the bands.

structural_notes: Navigation is a persistent left rail (or, in Arkime's case, a dark top strip of bare word tabs; either is idiomatic -- pick the rail here because the console has five destinations, not nine) listing the console's fixed destinations: workspace, capture search, profile library, format reference, regression suite. It never lists sessions -- sessions are not browsable in this category, they are produced by a query. A breadcrumb sits above every page title and is the only back-affordance the content area offers: Capture search / Result set / Session udp-a / Frame 3. The load-bearing pattern is query-then-master-detail-twice. A search form takes a display-filter expression plus a capture-window scope and is scoped by default to the most recently rotated segment, with an explicit control to widen to the whole stored capture set -- the result set does not exist until the query is submitted, and the count line above the table ('Showing N of M sessions') is how completeness is checked. A result row carries only session-level facts (session id, protocol, frame count) and clicking it opens that session's frame ledger; the ledger is one row per frame in stored arrival order (message id, tick, fragment index / fragment count, byte length) and carries no payload; selecting a ledger row binds a byte inspector to that one frame, which shows the offset/hex/ASCII triad for that frame alone and never a concatenation. Detail surfaces are collapsible white cards of right-aligned labels against blue values, not forms. The profile library is a dense table sorted by last modified by default, with sort-by-status and search-by-name as the two ways of surfacing the profile actually in force; a profile record is a read-only parameter list (mode, key, protocol order, strict fragment drop) and superseded profiles open to a withheld-parameters notice rather than an empty table. The format reference is a sequential prose document with prev/next paging and no jump index. Vocabulary and units, all drawn from the data and the domain: capture set, capture segment, capture window, display filter, session, session_id, protocol (lowercase tcp / udp), frame, frame ledger, tick (a bare monotonic integer, never a timestamp or a duration), message_id, fragment index / fragment count, payload_hex (lowercase, even-length, byte-pair grouped), reassembly, delivered, dropped, missing fragments, replay order, replay scheduler, protocol priority, protocol matrix, profile, in-force profile, regression case, refusal case, invariant case, ValueError. Counts are plain integers with no unit; byte payloads are described in bytes; ordering is stated in words next to the column ('tick, then protocol priority, then session_id') rather than implied. Nothing in the chrome is branded: no product wordmark in the rail, just a small neutral mark and the console name in text.
